name: Altruism
summary: Altruism is the moral view that the good of others, not one's own benefit, is the end of right conduct, so that people are obliged to give, help and sacrifice for others without expecting return. As a social outlook it prizes benevolence, charity, mutual care and service over self-interest, and contrasts itself with egoism.
scope: The ethical doctrine and social ethic of altruism: the view, coined by Auguste Comte as the antithesis of egoism, that moral action aims at the good of others and that one has a duty to benefit them (Britannica; Palmer; McConnell). It covers the Comtean/positivist 'live for others' ethic and its later philosophical defenders, treated as a view of how people and society should relate. It excludes biological altruism (an evolutionary term for fitness-costly behaviour, SEP), effective altruism and mutual aid (separate catalog entries), and books that merely use the word in a title for a college or institution's history.
